chunks: And it was also narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Abū Usāmah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: concerning

Regarding the mouse, the cat, the hen, the bird, and the dog, he said: “If it has not decomposed, or the taste of the water has not changed, then five buckets will suffice you. But if the water has changed, then draw from it until the odor goes away.”

key_terms.تَغَيَّرَ: changed, meaning the water was altered by impurity
key_terms.خَمْسُ دِلَاءٍ: five buckets, the stated amount sufficient in a specific case
key_terms.طَعْمُ: taste, one of the indicators of change in the water
key_terms.ٱلرِّيحُ: odor, whose disappearance indicates completion of the purification process
key_terms.ٱلسِّنَّوْرِ: the cat, listed among the animals discussed in the ruling
key_terms.ٱلْفَأْرَةِ: the mouse, mentioned as a source of contamination in the water
key_terms.ٱلْمَاءِ: the water whose purity and alteration are being assessed

ai.seo_question: How should water be purified if a mouse, cat, bird, hen, or dog contaminates it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on purifying water affected by impurities from certain animals. If the impurity has not decomposed or altered the water’s taste, removing five buckets is sufficient; if the water’s condition has changed, more must be removed until the smell disappears.
